keys.statement: Acetic acid and water form no azeotrope but are close-boiling, so heterogeneous azeotropic distillation is used; with n-butyl acetate as entrainer a cited study cut annual cost by 55% against plain distillation, and dilute feeds often add a preconcentrator column.

plain.title: Acetic acid from water: heterogeneous azeotropic distillation with butyl acetate as entrainer
plain.when: Acetic acid and water form no azeotrope but are close-boiling.
plain.do: Use heterogeneous azeotropic distillation with n-butyl acetate as entrainer. For dilute feeds add a preconcentrator column.
plain.why: The entrainer carries water overhead as a heterogeneous azeotrope that splits in a decanter.
plain.check: In CHEPTA, set phases: "VLL" and check the water-ester split in the decanter.
plain.result: A study cited by Valentini & Vaccaro 2020, not read by Lab, cut annual cost by 55% against plain distillation.

decisions.mechanism: The entrainer carries water overhead as a heterogeneous azeotrope.
decisions.operation: Heterogeneous azeotropic distillation with an ester entrainer.

keys.statement: For aqueous solvent mixtures with several azeotropes, hybrid extractive-heterogeneous azeotropic distillation uses the water already present as entrainer, so no new solvent or azeotrope is added.

plain.title: Solvent waste with several azeotropes and water: use the water as the entrainer
plain.when: An aqueous solvent waste holds several azeotropes.
plain.do: Use hybrid extractive-heterogeneous azeotropic distillation, with the water already present as the entrainer.
plain.why: Water acts as the extractive agent and forms separable heterogeneous azeotropes, so no new component is added.
plain.check: Map the azeotropes of the mixture first.

decisions.obstacle: Several azeotropes in a solvent waste.
decisions.mechanism: Water acts as extractive agent and forms separable heterogeneous azeotropes.

keys.statement: The required purity can change the best technology: for isobutanol at 98.8 wt% pervaporation ranked above azeotropic distillation, while at 99.9 wt% distillation-assisted pervaporation with heat integration was clearly best.

plain.title: The purity target can change the best dehydration technology
plain.when: You choose a dehydration technology (for isobutanol, in a study cited by Valentini & Vaccaro 2020).
plain.do: Compare the technologies at the actual purity target.
plain.why: Membrane area and distillation duty scale differently with purity.
plain.check: Rerun the comparison at your own purity.
plain.result: At 98.8 wt% isobutanol pervaporation ranked above azeotropic distillation; at 99.9 wt% distillation-assisted pervaporation with heat integration was clearly best (a cited result, not read by Lab).

keys.statement: Screen heterogeneous entrainers by the width of the miscibility gap, the composition of the azeotrope they form, and the temperature gaps to the other azeotropes in the system.

plain.title: Screening heterogeneous entrainers: miscibility gap, azeotrope composition, temperature gaps
plain.when: You choose among many candidate entrainers.
plain.do: Screen on three criteria before simulating: the width of the miscibility gap (the two-liquid region), the composition of the azeotrope each forms, and the temperature gaps to the other azeotropes.
plain.why: These properties decide the decanter split and whether the column is feasible.
plain.check: Compute the three criteria with the property method for each candidate.

keys.statement: Heterogeneous azeotropic distillation can be built as a dividing-wall column; a cited solvent-recovery case saved about 33% energy and 20% annual cost.

plain.title: Heterogeneous azeotropic distillation can be built as a dividing-wall column
plain.when: Azeotropic distillation uses a lot of energy.
plain.do: Consider a heterogeneous azeotropic dividing-wall column (one shell with an internal wall).
plain.check: Compare with the two-column process on the same basis.
plain.result: About 33% less energy and 20% lower annual cost in a solvent-recovery case cited by Valentini & Vaccaro 2020, not read by Lab.
